storyline.latest_title: Moonlight & Mayhem (Raccoon Heist by Codex + GPT-5.6 Sol Ultra)

prior_narrative.tldr: OpenAI's GPT-5.6 family — Luna, Terra, and Sol — had been gated to trusted partners only before reaching general availability. That two-week restricted window closed on July 9.
prior_narrative.whats_new: GPT-5.6 — Luna, Terra, and Sol — reached general availability on July 9, with Simon Willison's independent GA writeup landing the same day and a next-day AINews recap widening independent confirmation.
prior_narrative.why_it_matters: The GA move ends the restricted-partner window and adds a three-tier lineup (Luna/Terra/Sol) with per-tier pricing, so integrations built against the restricted tier should re-check access and re-evaluate cost/latency against the new tiers before defaulting to the largest model.

beats.headline: Luna, Terra, and Sol open to everyone with tiered per-token pricing
beats.summary: Luna prices at $1/$6 per 1M input/output tokens as the smallest of the three sizes; a next-day AINews recap widened independent confirmation of the same release.

open_questions: What are Terra's and Sol's exact per-token prices relative to Luna's $1/$6?
Does GA access carry the same safety commitments OpenAI touted at the model's unveiling?
prior_narrative.take_for_builders: If you were on the restricted GPT-5.6 tier, re-check your access and quota now that GA is open, and benchmark Luna's $1/$6-per-1M-token tier against your current model before defaulting to Sol for cost-sensitive agent loops.
